paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. When Ahaziah got hurt, he had a real question: will I get better? He just took it to the wrong place, Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron (2 Kings 1:2). The LORD's question through Elijah, "Is it because there is no God in Israel…" (2 Kings 1:3), is aimed right at that. Where we carry our biggest worries says who we really trust.

Now look at the three captains. The first two came up the hill barking orders at a man of God, and the king's whole plan was to make the LORD's word come down off that hill (2 Kings 1:9-12). The third captain came on his knees, saying, "may my life… be precious in your sight" (2 Kings 1:13-14). Friend, you can't boss God's word around, you can't outvote it, and you can't send fifty men to arrest it. You can only come humbly, and I think that third captain knew it.

And the word the LORD spoke didn't budge. Ahaziah heard it by messenger, then again face to face, and both times it was the same: "You will surely die." (2 Kings 1:16). Ahaziah died "according to the word of the LORD" (2 Kings 1:17). So when something hits you, baker, take it to the God who said it and does it. His word still stands when nobody wants to hear it, and that's good news for everybody who trusts it.
